The proposed answer, q^{D(r-1)}, matches the structure I'd expect, but I could not confirm it against a source. This check is a heuristic one.

The proposal's reasoning is the analogue of Hida theory. Classically, the ordinary part of level Γ1(Np^r) has rank growing like p^{r-1} times the rank at level Np, once all p-power-order characters are included. In characteristic p, the wild diamond operators in W_r = ker((A/℘^r)^× → (A/℘)^×) act unipotently, so the eigensystems twisted by those characters collapse into a single eigensystem. The multiplicity should then be inflated by |W_r| = q^{D(r-1)}. This also gives ratio 1 at r = 1, as it must. The proposal's claim that the space is free over the group algebra of W_r is asserted rather than proved, but it fits this picture.

I cannot rule out that the true answer takes a different form. I do not remember the precise statement of the relevant theorem, so this verdict rests on the heuristic consistency above.
